Adam Murphy (present) |partner = |children = 1 |parents = |relations = |awards = |signature = |website = {{URL|http://www.flapperfilms.com}} |footnotes = }} '''Elizabeth Ward Gracen''' (born '''Elizabeth Grace Ward''', April 3, 1961) is an [[Americans|American]] actress and beauty pageant contestant who won the title of [[Miss America]] in 1982. == Early life and education == Elizabeth Grace Ward was born on April 3, 1961, in [[Ozark, Arkansas|Ozark]], [[Arkansas]], the daughter of Patricia Hampe, a nurse, and Jimmy Young Ward, a poultry worker. She was raised in [[Booneville, Arkansas]]. The family later moved to [[Russellville, Arkansas]], where Ward dated University of Arkansas trainer Mike Walker and graduated from [[Russellville High School (Arkansas)|Russellville High School]] in 1979.{{cite encyclopedia | title = Elizabeth Ward Gracen (1961–) | url = http://encyclopediaofarkansas.net/encyclopedia/entry-detail.aspx?entryID=2747 | encyclopedia = Encyclopedia of Arkansas | access-date = January 11, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120314045228/http://www.encyclopediaofarkansas.net/encyclopedia/entry-detail.aspx?entryID=2747 | archive-date = March 14, 2012 | url-status = dead }} She was a junior accounting major at [[Arkansas Tech University]] at the time she entered the Miss America contest.Thomas DeBlack. "A Century Forward: The Centennial History of Arkansas Tech University." Walsworth Publishing Company. 2016. Instead of returning to Arkansas Tech, she used her Miss America scholarship money to study acting at HB Studios in New York City. ==Career== ===Pageants and modeling=== Gracen won the titles of [[Miss Arkansas]] in 1981 and [[Miss America]] in 1982. After her yearlong work as Miss America, she enrolled in acting classes then relocated to [[California]] to pursue a film and television career. Gracen posed nude for ''[[Playboy]]'' magazine's May 1992 issue.{{cite journal| journal= [[Playboy]]| title= [Unknown]| pages= | issn= | date= May 1992| url= | access-date= }} ===Acting=== Gracen made her professional feature film debut in ''Three For The Road'' with [[Charlie Sheen]]. Her film credits also include a featured role in ''[[Marked for Death]]'', opposite [[Steven Seagal]], ''Pass The Ammo'' with [[Tim Curry]], and the CBS feature ''83 Hours Till Dawn'' with [[Peter Strauss]] and [[Robert Urich]]. Gracen starred in ''[[Lower Level]]'' and ''Discretion Assured'' with [[Michael York (actor)|Michael York]]. On television, Gracen has appeared in [[Shelley Duvall]]'s ''[[Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde]]'', [[Sidney Sheldon]]'s ''[[The Sands of Time (Sheldon novel)|The Sands of Time]]'' and ''Death of the Incredible Hulk''. She also appeared with a starring role in the series ''Extreme'' for NBC and the syndicated series ''[[Renegade (TV series)|Renegade]]'' and ''[[Queen of Swords (TV series)|Queen of Swords]]''. Gracen's best-known acting role has been as the recurring character, the Immortal [[Amanda (Highlander)|Amanda]], in the series ''[[Highlander: The Series]]'' and its spin-off series ''[[Highlander: The Raven]]''. [[File:Elizabeth Gracen by Gage Skidmore.jpg|right|thumb|Gracen, speaking about writing at [[TusCon]] 43 in Tucson, Arizona]] In December 1999, Gracen filed for bankruptcy protection. Afterward, Gracen was given a few television guest roles, and a supporting role in the made-for-television movie ''Interceptor Force 2'', before taking a long leave of absence from her acting career in 2002. Gracen began doing voiceover work for Blue Hours Productions, which has revived the classic radio anthology ''[[Suspense (radio drama)|Suspense]]'', which airs on [[Sirius XM]]. In 2012, Gracen did a character voice-over in the Malaysian animated science fiction film ''[[War of the Worlds: Goliath]]''. ===Directing, producing and writing=== In 2012, Gracen formed Flapper Films.{{cite news| first= Claudia| last= Palma| title=Lineage Performing Arts Center to screen documentary highlighting dancing with Parkinson's classes| url=http://www.pasadenastarnews.com/health/20150813/lineage-performing-arts-center-to-screen-documentary-highlighting-dancing-with-parkinsons-classes|accessdate=21 March 2016|work=The Pasadena Star-News|date=13 August 2015}} In 2014, she starred in ''Coherence'', a sci-fi indie thriller.{{cite news | last =Barnard | first = Linda | title =Coherence: Comet shakes things up in thriller: review | work= thestar.com| date =18 September 2016 | url =https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/movies/2014/09/18/coherence_comet_shakes_things_up_in_thriller_review.html | accessdate =14 July 2016}} In January 2016, Gracen established Flapper Press and self-published ''Shalilly'', a young adult fantasy novel.{{cite news | last = Keegan | first = Simon | title =Highlander star and Miss America Elizabeth Gracen launches new career as children's book author | work= mirror.co.uk| date =13 April 2016 | url =https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/highlander-star-miss-america-elizabeth-7744222| accessdate =14 July 2016}} Gracen made her directorial debut with a [[documentary film|documentary]] [[short film|short]], "The Damn Deal" about three young [[drag queen]]s from Arkansas who compete in female impersonator beauty pageants. ==Personal life== ===Marriages and family=== Gracen married Jon Birmingham in 1982, but they divorced in 1984.{{citation needed|date= March 2017}} In 1989, while filming ''[[Sundown: The Vampire in Retreat]]'', she met actor Brendan Hughes, and they married soon after.{{citation needed|date= March 2017}} They divorced in 1994. Gracen married Adam Murphy, and they have a daughter.{{citation needed|date= March 2017}} ===Affair with Bill Clinton=== According to Gracen, some time in 1983, she had a [[one-night stand]] with future President [[Bill Clinton]] when he was [[Governor of Arkansas]].{{cite news|title=Beauty queen apologises for tryst|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=uxUSAAAAIBAJ&pg=4296,5792168&dq=bill-clinton+elizabeth-ward&hl=en| work= [[Gainesville Sun]] |date=April 26, 1998| agency= Associated Press| access-date= March 15, 2017}}{{cite news|title=She hitched her star to a wagon for the love of Bill, Hillary put her goals on hold and move to Ark. stick|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/news/2000/02/08/2000-02-08_she_hitched_her_star_to_a_wa.html|work=[[New York Daily News]]|date=February 8, 2000|first=Helen|last=Kennedy}}{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} She was married at the time as was he. In 1992, rumors swirled that Gracen had conducted an affair with Bill Clinton.{{cite news |date= January 14, 1999 |url= http://home.hiwaay.net/~craigg/g4c/gracen.htm |title=Elizabeth Gracen: the Clinton reign of terror |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204003520/http://home.hiwaay.net/~craigg/g4c/gracen.htm |archivedate=February 4, 2009 }} At first, Gracen dismissed this claim (as requested by Clinton's campaign manager [[Mickey Kantor]]); however, in spring 1998 Gracen recanted her six-year-old denial and stated she had a one-night stand with Clinton in 1982.{{cite web| title= All the President's Women – Elizabeth Ward Gracen |url=http://www.comedyontap.com/presgirls/ward.html |work=Comedy on Tap |url-status=dead |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20090213170931/http://comedyontap.com/presgirls/ward.html |archivedate=February 13, 2009 }} After claiming this, Independent Counsel [[Kenneth Starr]], who was investigating Clinton in the [[Clinton v. Jones|Paula Jones lawsuit]], issued a subpoena to have her testify to her claim in court.{{cite news| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/special/clinton/stories/subpoena122498.htm | work=The Washington Post | date=December 24, 1998|title=Big Year for the Bad News Bearers}} However, Gracen eluded the subpoena and was at one point able to avoid it because ''[[Highlander: The Raven]]'' was being filmed out of the country. Paula Jones' legal team was also unable to track down Gracen because she had made unscheduled trips to [[Las Vegas]] and the Caribbean. == Filmography == * ''[[Three for the Road]]'' (1987) Nadine * ''[[Pass the Ammo]]'' (1988) Christie Lynn * ''[[The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde]]'' (1989) * ''[[Lisa (1990 film)|Lisa]]'' (1989) Mary * ''[[The Death of the Incredible Hulk]]'' (1990) Jasmin * ''[[Marked for Death]]'' (1990) Melissa * ''[[The Flash]]'' (1990 TV Series) 1 episode - Celia Wayne * ''[[83 Hours 'Til Dawn]]'' (1990) Maria Ranfield * ''[[Sundown: The Vampire in Retreat]]'' (1991) Alice * ''[[Lower Level]]'' (1992) Hillary * ''[[The Sands of Time (film)|The Sands of Time]]'' (1992) * ''Final Mission'' (1993) Caitlin Cole * ''[[Time Trax]]'' episode 7 (1993) Sydney * ''[[Discretion Assured]]'' (1993) Miranda * ''[[Highlander: The Series]]'' (1992–1998) [[Amanda (Highlander)|Amanda]] * ''[[Murder, She Wrote]]'' (1994) Michelle Scarlotti * ''[[The Expert (1995 film)|The Expert]]'' (1995) Liz Pierce * ''[[Extreme (1995 TV series)|Extreme]]'' (1995) Callie Manners * ''[[Kounterfeit]]'' (1996) Bridgette * ''[[Highlander: The Raven]]'' (1998–1999) [[Amanda (Highlander)|Amanda]] * ''[[Queen of Swords (TV series)|Queen of Swords]]'' "Counterfeit Queen" (2000) Carlotta * ''[[Charmed]]'' "Bite Me" (2002) Vampire Queen * ''[[Interceptor Force 2 (movie)|Interceptor Force 2]]'' (2002) Adriana Sikes * ''[[War of the Worlds: Goliath]]'' (2012) Lt.
